title: Written mention extraction envelope v4
description: What one model call may say about a bounded batch of source records. v4 is the Cardinal Ontology specification's §5.2 output contract: every mention names which of the eight immutable roots it believes it is and how confidently, which supplied parent it fits under (parent_candidate_id — an echo of a request-supplied id, never an invented one; the Python validator enforces the echo), a §5.3 missing-parent proposal when no supplied parent fits, the user predicate it would ground, and ranked alternatives. Every guard on an EXTRACTED mention is unchanged. Grammar-shape rule, learned twice now (patterns 2026-08-19; the first draft of this file 2026-08-21, which collapsed generation to under 10 tokens/sec): xgrammar 0.2.3 is trusted ONLY with the shapes this stack has measured — pure string enums, [scalar,null] type unions, and arrays of objects with required properties. No optional properties, no null inside an enum, no anyOf-nullable objects. 'none' as an explicit enum member stands in for null, and a proposal travels in a maxItems-1 array instead of a nullable object.

items.description: Two, not four. The gateway accepts at most two indexed items and the contract calibrates for two; the schema is set to the same number so a third cannot be emitted by a model that misread its instructions. Raising it is a schema version change, which is correct: batch size is part of the output contract, not a runtime dial.

surface.description: Kept alongside the offsets during the first evaluation so the gateway can check surface == source[start:end]. One of the two may be dropped later if multilingual offset accuracy proves reliable; they must not both remain permanently without an accuracy reason. No pattern here on purpose: xgrammar 0.2.3's token matcher leaks on patterned strings (accepts token paths outside the string language, then admits schema-illegal continuations downstream — measured 2026-08-19 against the live endpoint and reproduced locally). The control-character and not-all-whitespace guards live in written_ontology.mention_extract_v2, the layer for what the schema cannot safely express.

start.description: Unicode code point offset, not a byte or UTF-16 offset. A surrogate-pair or combining-mark string makes the three disagree, and the gateway's equality check is what would fail.

family_hypothesis.description: music_recording is deliberately absent. 0221 removed recordings from the versioned ontology because identity is not vocabulary; a model emitting that family would reopen the minting route it closed.

english_label.description: The term in English, where the surface is not already English. Stored beside the original rather than joined into one string, because 'Jay Chou (周杰倫)' is a rendering and a rendering belongs where something is drawn. Null when the model has no English form.

original_label.description: The term in its original language, where the surface is the English one. The pair is what lets a surface show either or both.

relation_hypotheses.description: At most two relations to other terms. Bounded because a mention that could relate to everything is describing nothing.

selected_cardinal.description: The root the model selects, or 'none' when it cannot say — an explicit member rather than null, because a null inside an enum is not a shape this stack trusts xgrammar with. The validator maps 'none' to absence.

cardinal_confidence.description: Belief in the selected root, 0 when selected_cardinal is 'none'. The full distribution was cut deliberately: an object of optional numbers is what collapsed generation; the runner-up readings live in alternatives instead.

parent_candidate_id.description: The id of the supplied parent candidate this term fits under, or null. MUST be echoed from the request's parent_candidates (§5.2, No model IDs); the Python validator refuses an id that was not supplied.

missing_parent_proposals.description: §5.3: at most one proposal, only when no supplied parent fits. An array rather than a nullable object — arrays of objects are a shape generation is proven on. Never alongside parent_candidate_id.

candidate_user_predicate.description: The user predicate this evidence would ground, from the closed user registry (predicate-v2.0), or 'none'. A like grounds interested_in; nothing here may claim practices from a watch.

alternatives.description: §5.2, Alternatives preserved: the ranked other readings, so the model does not choose the globally most famous entity merely to avoid provisional state.

relation_hypothesis.description: A relation the model believes holds between this mention and another term — 'Luffy part_of_franchise One Piece'. The object is a bare label, never an id: the model does not know what has been minted and must never choose one. Optional by the owner's decision: an inferred term needs no tether to be admitted, and a relation is recorded when the model has one rather than demanded before it may speak.

mention_inferred.description: A term the model asserts from its own knowledge — the franchise behind a character, the artist behind a track, the English name of a foreign one. It has no span because it is not in the text, so `start`, `end` and `source_field_index` are absent rather than nulled: a reader must not be able to mistake an inferred mention for an extracted one whose offsets happened to be zero. `source_field` is the constant 'inferred', which is how the variant is told apart, the same mechanism `mention_tag` uses.

missing_parent_proposal.description: §5.3's missing-parent proposal contract. The validator rejects a circular definition, a proposal whose only example child is the proposed leaf itself, and a broader_parent_id that was not supplied in the request.

broader_parent_id.description: An echoed supplied id, or null for a root-level parent.

alternative_reading.description: One other thing this mention could denote. The family enum is the mention variants' own, and the compiler asserts they cannot drift apart.
